surface: global shell › sidebar + project navigation column (every project page)
inventoryRow: Global shell, desktop sidebar, phone navigation drawer, top bar
evidence: scratchpad/walk/w3-keyboard/ (focus logs per key press)
No skip link or other bypass: first Tab on /app goes to the theme button, then Home, Projects, New project
T03: 20 Tab stops from the sidebar Kitchen link to the first canvas control ('Insert before Markdown')
T04: 26 Tab stops from the sidebar Client migration link to the first task title
T05/T09: after focus is reset on the Archive page, 13 Tab stops of project navigation and header before the first archive row
repro: 3. press Tab repeatedly, open Kitchen from the sidebar with Enter
4. keep pressing Tab and count stops until focus reaches anything inside the Work canvas
expected: A keyboard user can jump past the repeated workspace sidebar and project navigation to the page's main content in one or two key presses.
actual: There is no skip link or landmark shortcut exposed; every project page requires walking the global sidebar (6-9 stops), the project navigation (8-12 stops) and the header (3 stops) before any content.
heuristic: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks; Nielsen #7 Flexibility and efficiency of use

surface: app-wide › focus indicator
inventoryRow: Global shell, desktop sidebar, phone navigation drawer, top bar
evidence: Computed styles: sidebar links, theme button, New project, project-nav page links, workstream links, More project actions, task checkboxes/titles/Delete, Add task, task inputs, drawer fields, Archive Restore, Agents checkboxes => outline: auto 1px rgb(16,16,16) (browser default ring)

Computed styles: page-settings gear, Add workstream, Undo/Redo, insertion points, section chrome (Move/Collapse/Rename/Remove/Resize), dialog fields and buttons, Markdown Edit/Preview/Save => outline: solid 2px rgb(255,159,107) with 0-4px offset
Shortcut picker dialog mixes both: 'Add a section'/'Back' orange ring, every 'Add' button default ring (022-t07-03-add-focus.png)
t01-01-newproject-focus.png, t03-01-insert-focus.png, t03-04-addtask-focus.png, t06-02-save-focus.png
repro: 2. open /app, press Tab into the sidebar and open Kitchen
3. continue Tab through project navigation, header and canvas, observing the ring on each control
expected: One recognisable focus indicator across the app, so the keyboard user learns what 'focused' looks like once.
actual: Two unrelated indicators alternate from stop to stop: a thin white/black browser ring hugging the element and a 2px orange outline with an offset; neighbouring controls in the same panel or dialog use different ones.
heuristic: Nielsen #4 Consistency and standards; WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible (indicator is present but inconsistent)

surface: route changes from in-page controls › New project Create, section-removal notice 'Open Archive', project navigation page links, Settings › 'AI & Agents' link
inventoryRow: Global shell, desktop sidebar, phone navigation drawer, top bar
evidence: T01: Enter on Create (empty seed) navigates to the new project; document.activeElement = BODY (002-t01-03-after-create.png)
T05: Enter on 'Open Archive' in the removal notice -> /pages/archive, activeElement = BODY
T09: Enter on project-navigation 'Archive' link -> activeElement = BODY
T10 (agent-heavy): Enter on 'AI & Agents' on /settings -> activeElement = BODY
Contrast: Enter on a sidebar project link or the sidebar Settings link keeps focus on that link
repro: 2. open /projects/project-renovation via the sidebar with the keyboard
3. Tab to the project navigation 'Archive' link and press Enter
expected: After following a link or completing a create, focus lands somewhere meaningful (the new page's heading or the control that was used), the same way each time.
actual: Focus is dropped to the document body on these route changes, while sidebar links keep focus on the link; the user cannot tell where the next Tab will start and screen-reader users get no landing point.
heuristic: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order; Nielsen #4 Consistency and standards

surface: project workspace › Archive page › archived item Restore
evidence: T05: Enter on 'Restore saved content for Markdown' -> row disappears, activeElement = BODY (017-t05-05-after-restore.png)
T09: Enter on 'Restore Legacy attic' -> activeElement = BODY, still BODY after 800 ms (027-t09-03-after.png)
repro: 2. open Home renovation › Archive with the keyboard
3. Tab to 'Restore Legacy attic' and press Enter
expected: After restoring, focus stays in the archive list (next item, the list, or the success notice) so the user can continue or follow 'Open Legacy attic'.
actual: The restored row is removed and focus falls to the body; the success notice in the header is not focused and the user must Tab again from the project navigation.
heuristic: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order

surface: project navigation › page settings panel › 'Show Reflections page' checkbox
inventoryRow: Project navigation and page settings panel
evidence: T08: Space on 'Show Reflections page' -> page hidden, activeElement = BODY (still BODY after 1 s) (025-t08-03-hidden.png)
T08: Space again to re-enable -> activeElement = BODY again
The checkbox itself remains on screen in the same place in both states
repro: 2. open Home renovation, Tab to 'Project page settings for Home renovation' and press Enter
3. Tab to 'Show Reflections page' and press Space
expected: Toggling a checkbox leaves focus on that checkbox, so it can be toggled back or the next one reached.
actual: Focus is lost on every toggle; the user must press Tab/Shift+Tab to find the checkbox again before each change.
heuristic: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order; WCAG 3.2.2 On Input (unexpected context change)

surface: project header › More project actions panel
evidence: Probe: Enter on 'More project actions' opens the inline panel (029-probe-more-menu.png); Tab into Name field; Escape closes the panel (aria-expanded=false) and activeElement = BODY (030-probe-more-escape.png)
repro: 2. open Kitchen and Tab to 'More project actions'
3. press Enter, then Tab once into the panel
expected: Closing the panel with Escape returns focus to the 'More project actions' button that opened it.
actual: The panel closes but focus goes to the document body.
heuristic: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order (focus return after dismissing a disclosure)

surface: sidebar › New project inline form
inventoryRow: Global shell, desktop sidebar, phone navigation drawer, top bar
evidence: T01 step 3: Enter on 'New project' shows the Project name textbox and Create button but activeElement stays on the '+' button
repro: 3. Tab to 'New project' (+) and press Enter
expected: Opening the form puts the caret in the name field so the user can type straight away.
actual: Focus remains on the '+' trigger; an extra Tab is needed before typing.
heuristic: Nielsen #7 Flexibility and efficiency of use

surface: sidebar › New project '+' button; Archive page › 'Restore' text buttons
inventoryRow: Global shell, desktop sidebar, phone navigation drawer, top bar
evidence: Rect of focused 'New project' button: 26x15 px (t01-01-newproject-focus.png shows the focus ring squeezed around the '+')
Rect of focused 'Restore Legacy attic' button: 43x20 px; 'Restore saved content for Markdown': 127x20 px (t09-02-restore-focus.png)
repro: 2. open /app and Tab to 'New project'; read its bounding rect
3. open Home renovation › Archive and Tab to 'Restore Legacy attic'; read its bounding rect
expected: Primary actions are at least 24 px tall so they are easy to hit and the focus ring has room.
actual: These controls are 15-20 px tall; the focus ring on '+' is cramped against the glyph.
heuristic: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)

surface: /app dashboard › landmarks
evidence: ARIA snapshot of /app: 'main' contains a second 'main' (main > main > heading 'Home'); also seen on overdue-chaos. Project pages have a single main.
expected: One main landmark per page.
actual: The dashboard exposes a main landmark nested inside another main landmark.
heuristic: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships

surface: project navigation › Add workstream dialog › Parent
evidence: T02: opened from /projects/project-kitchen; Parent select preset to 'Home renovation', helper 'Inside Home renovation' (004-t02-03-dialog.png)
repro: 3. Tab to 'Add workstream' and press Enter
expected: When I am looking at Kitchen and add a workstream, it is placed under Kitchen unless I choose otherwise.
actual: The parent defaults to the root project regardless of the page I am on; a user who just types a name and presses Enter creates it in the wrong place.
heuristic: Nielsen #2 Match between system and the real world

surface: project canvas › section chrome tab stops
evidence: T04 tab log: Markdown section = Insert before, Move, Collapse, Rename, Remove, Edit, Resize (7 stops for one Edit button); Task List section = Insert before, Move, Collapse, Rename, Remove before the 'Add a task' field, Resize after
T03/T05/T06/T07: same pattern on Kitchen; reaching the second section's content costs ~12 chrome stops
repro: 2. open Client migration from the sidebar
3. Tab from the header into the canvas and list the stops
expected: Moving through the canvas by keyboard reaches each section's content quickly; arranging chrome does not dominate the tab sequence.
actual: Every section inserts 5-6 chrome stops (insert, move, collapse, rename, remove, resize) around 1-2 content controls, so ordinary work (editing text, reaching a task) requires long Tab runs and frequent overshoots (T03, T04, T05 and T06 each overshot).
heuristic: Nielsen #7 Flexibility and efficiency of use; Nielsen #8 Aesthetic and minimalist design

surface: Task List section › add task field
evidence: T03: after typing 'Paint' Enter / 'Bulbs' Enter, a Task details drawer for the new task was open and the list narrowed (008-t03-07-both-done.png)
Verification on fresh seed: 'Task details' count 0 before, 1 after a single Enter in the add field
repro: 2. open Kitchen, Tab to the Task List 'Add a task' field
3. type a title and press Enter
expected: Quick-adding several tasks keeps the list as it is; details open only when asked for.
actual: Each add selects the new task and opens its details drawer beside the list, halving the row width and adding the drawer's controls to the tab sequence.
heuristic: Nielsen #3 User control and freedom

surface: /app dashboard › Today and Upcoming widgets › task items
evidence: T04: ARIA of Today › Overdue lists 'Export legacy records … Client migration · 2026-08-18' as plain listitem text with a time; no link/button; Tab never stops on them (009-t04-00.png)
repro: 3. Tab through the page; inspect the Today widget's items
expected: An overdue task shown on the dashboard can be opened from there.
actual: The items are not interactive; the user must go to the project through the sidebar and tab through the whole canvas to find the same task.
heuristic: Nielsen #7 Flexibility and efficiency of use

surface: Task List section › Task detail drawer › tab order
evidence: T04: after Enter on 'Export legacy records, open details', 13 Tab stops (Delete plus checkbox/title/Delete of 4 other rows) before 'Close task details', Title, Priority, Due date
repro: 2. open Client migration, Tab to the first task title and press Enter
3. press Tab repeatedly until focus enters the drawer
expected: After opening a task's details, the details are the next thing the keyboard reaches.
actual: The drawer comes after every remaining row in the list; with a long list the details are far away and focus stays on the title by design.
heuristic: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order

surface: Task detail drawer › Status / Project / Priority values
evidence: 013-t04-04-date-focus.png: drawer shows 'Status in_progress', 'Project project-client-migration', Priority select 'high' while the row says 'High Priority'
expected: The drawer speaks in the same words as the rest of the app (e.g. the project's name, a readable status).
actual: Internal identifiers and enum spellings are shown verbatim.
heuristic: Nielsen #2 Match between system and the real world

surface: Section creation dialog › Add shortcut › return focus
evidence: T07: after Enter on the Task List 'Add' in the shortcut picker, focus returned to 'Insert before Markdown' at y=1008 in a 900 px viewport; the page was not scrolled and the focused control was off screen (023-t07-04-after.png)
repro: 2. open Kitchen, Tab to 'Insert before Markdown', Enter
4. Tab to the Task List (Home renovation · Home) 'Add' and press Enter
5. compare the focused element's rect with the viewport
expected: After the dialog closes, the focused control is visible on screen.
actual: Focus sits on an insertion point that is pushed below the fold by the tall new shortcut; no focus indicator is visible anywhere on screen.
heuristic: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)

surface: Shortcut picker 'Add' buttons; Settings › AI & Agents 'Revoke' buttons and permission checkboxes
evidence: Shortcut picker ARIA: nine buttons all named 'Add' (two sources named 'Markdown', two 'Task List', two 'Reflections')
agent-heavy /settings/agents ARIA: three 'Revoke' buttons and three sets of checkboxes named 'Read projects', 'Modify tasks' etc. with no agent name in the accessible name or a group label
repro: 2. open the shortcut picker from a Kitchen insertion point and read button names
3. seed agent-heavy, open Settings › AI & Agents and read button/checkbox names
expected: Each control's name says what it acts on (which source, which agent) when read out of visual context.
actual: Repeated identical names; a keyboard/screen-reader user tabbing through hears 'Add', 'Add', 'Add' or 'Revoke', 'Revoke' with nothing to tell them apart.
heuristic: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.6 Headings and Labels; SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships

surface: project workspace › Archive page › archived item row focus order
evidence: T05/T09 tab log: in each row, 'Work canvas' (origin line) and 'Open … history' links come before the Restore control, although Restore is drawn top-right on the item's title line (016-t05-04-restore-focus.png)
repro: 3. Tab into the first archive item
expected: Focus moves in the order the row is read visually: title line action first, then details below.
actual: Focus jumps down to the origin and history links, then back up to Restore at the top right.
heuristic: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order; SC 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence

surface: project workspace › Archive page › 'Origin: … / Work canvas / …' link
evidence: 016-t05-04-restore-focus.png and 026-t09-01-archive.png: 'Work canvas' inside the grey Origin line has the same colour and no underline as the surrounding text; it is only discoverable when Tab lands on it
repro: 3. look at the Origin line of 'Legacy attic'
expected: A link is recognisable as a link without having to focus it.
actual: The link is visually identical to the breadcrumb text around it.
heuristic: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color / link distinguishability; Nielsen #6 Recognition rather than recall

surface: Settings › AI & Agents
evidence: T10: full Tab pass through /settings/agents: only permission checkboxes and Revoke buttons (16 stops), then wraps to the top bar; no connect/add control
Development panel (Ctrl+Shift+D) 'Agent connection' region is read-only (Copy token) and says permissions live in Settings
No other Settings entry mentions connecting an agent
repro: 3. Tab through the whole page looking for a way to connect a new agent
expected: Next to the list of what agents may do, a way to connect a new agent (or at least instructions for doing so).
actual: Permissions are visible and editable, but there is no control or guidance in the product UI for connecting a new agent; the task cannot be completed.
heuristic: Nielsen #10 Help and documentation; Nielsen #3 User control and freedom
